newsitem.title: GERMANY: German defence minister rejects smaller army call.
newsitem.headline: German defence minister rejects smaller army call.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Sunday an opposition call to reduce the army's size and cut the conscription period to six from 10 months would destroy its structure.

Warning the Bundeswehr's conscription-based structure would collapse if recruits were drafted into service for less than 10 months, Ruehe said in an interview with ZDF television the army could absorb cuts in material procurements but not manpower.

"It would be highly damaging for the Bundeswehr," Ruehe said of a proposal by Rudolf Scharping, parliamentary leader of the Social Democrats, to cut conscription to six months. "That would destroy the Bundeswehr as we now know it."
In January, German combat troops begin their first mission abroad since World War Two when 3,300 soldiers join NATO-led forces in Bosnia.
Germany's defence budget has been reduced in recent years, but Ruehe and many other political leaders have fought off calls to cut the army's size from its current 340,000.
That figure comprises 200,000 career soldiers and 140,000 conscripts.
Until recently, politicians across the spectrum have seen the draft as a guarantee the military forces will remain bound into a democratic society.
But now many of Germany's Western defence partners are now in the process of switching from conscript armies to leaner professional forces.

"We were able to cut to 10 months (from 15 months) because we are no longer in the middle of the Cold War," Ruehe said. "But you cannot properly train soldiers for a modern army with just six months' training."
